Ottawa promises reform to spur competition in the banking sector
sum: Ottawa is promising legislative changes to boost competition in Canada’s banking sector in the federal budget released Thursday, aiming to make it easier for new financial institutions to enter the market and gain a foothold.

The government will change the law that governs Canada’s banking regulator, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, to add a “secondary competition objective” to its mandate, the budget says. The current OSFI mandate focuses solely on maintaining a stable and sound financial system.
Further amendments to the acts governing banks, trust companies and insurers will establish a one-year timeline for making decisions on applications to create new banks, the budget says.

OSFI superintendent Peter Routledge has already been keenly focused on bringing competition and innovation into Canada’s highly concentrated banking sector. Canada’s banking industry is dominated by the Big Six banks – Royal Bank of Canada, Toronto-Dominion Bank, Bank of Nova Scotia, Bank of Montreal, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and National Bank of Canada – that hold more than 90-per-cent market share.
In June, Mr. Routledge launched a pilot project that could strip years off the process to become a bank in a bid to bring more competitors into the market.

Over the next decade, OSFI will have to regulate through a period of immense change in the financial sector, Mr. Routledge said in an interview in October. “Canadians want more competition,” he said at the time.

Thursday’s budget also seeks to allow more flexible ownership structures for smaller banks, making it easier for them to grow larger in a market that is highly concentrated and dominated by Canada’s Big Six lenders.

items.t: Can Mulvihill Bank ETF (TSX:MBNK) Maintain Its Distribution Momentum?
sum: - Mulvihill Canadian Bank ETF declared a five-cent monthly distribution.
- Holdings centre on six major Canadian banks, with options used to add income.

Mulvihill Canadian Bank ETF (TSX:MBNK) MBNK (TSX:MBNK) declared its monthly cash distribution in a release from Mulvihill Capital Management Inc. dated, setting the payment at five cents per share. The distribution is payable to shareholders of record, and it matches the amount shown in the manager's two previous monthly notices, which means the income stream has stayed level since the notices that preceded it. The announcement also offers a fresh read on sentiment toward exchange-traded funds across the TSX.

The steady payment is the main news in the announcement, but it also offers a chance to look at how this relatively new listing works. The fund launched on the Toronto Stock Exchange and is built around the common shares of six large Canadian banks, supplemented by an option-writing program intended to generate extra income.

According to the latest release, the record date falls and the payment follows about a week later. The preceding notice, issued, set the same five-cent amount for payment, and the notice before that, issued, did likewise for payment. A consistent cadence of five cents each month has therefore been declared across three consecutive announcements. These details form part of the latest disclosure from Mulvihill Canadian Bank ETF (TSX:MBNK) MBNK (TSX:MBNK) .

The announcements do not describe the source of the cash. Distributions from a fund like this can combine dividends received from the underlying shares, option premiums and, in some cases, a return of capital. The composition affects how the amounts are taxed under Canada Revenue Agency rules, and the formal breakdown appears on the tax slips that are issued after period end rather than in the monthly notices.

The fund's launch release, issued, stated that the portfolio consists mainly of the common shares of six Canadian banks: Bank of Montreal, The Bank of Nova Scotia, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, National Bank of Canada, Royal Bank of Canada and The Toronto-Dominion Bank. Those institutions form the core of the Canadian financial system, and they are among the largest constituents of the S&P/TSX Composite Index.

BMO stock: Stonepeak completes CAD 14.5 billion finance sale
sum: Bank of Montreal stock remains in focus after BMO completed the sale of its Transportation Finance and Vendor Finance businesses to Stonepeak on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Stonepeak said the businesses will operate as Longview Capital Solutions, with customer relationships and service arrangements continuing during the transition.

At closing, BMO transferred approximately 75 percent, or CAD 11 billion, of an estimated CAD 14.5 billion combined loan and lease portfolio to Stonepeak. The remaining balances are expected to transfer in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, subject to customary conditions.

The transaction is expected to improve BMO's common equity Tier 1 ratio by approximately 23 basis points in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. BMO retains a 19.9 percent interest in the Stonepeak-managed entity, preserving participation in the businesses' future development.

Stonepeak said Longview will operate as an independent commercial equipment finance company. Customers will continue working with the same experienced teams and systems, while BMO provides transition services and continues servicing and originating current and future loans on Longview's behalf. The details were reported in Stonepeak's announcement.
